newsitem.title: CANADA: Six yards to compete in Canada oil project tender.
newsitem.headline: Six yards to compete in Canada oil project tender.

text.p: Energy firms proposing the Terra Nova oil project off Canada's east coast said on Thursday they selected six shipyards to tender on the design and construction of their floating production facility's steel hull.

The companies said shipyards picked to bid on the project included Astano Shipyard of Spain, Harland and Wolff SHI Ltd of the United Kingdom, Mitsui Engineering & Shipbuilding Co Ltd of Japan, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd of Japan, Samsung Heavy Industries Co Ltd of Korea and Daewoo Heavy Industries of South Korea.
The project's proponents, led by Petro-Canada, said 31 shipyards were orginially invited to submit expressions of interest, including some from Canada and the United States.
The two invited Canadian yards could not build the hull size required and declined to participated in the bid, the Terra Nova partners said.

Terra Nova is the second major offshore oil project off Canada's east coast. Located 350 km (217 miles) southeast of the province of Newfoundland, the field harbors an estimated 400 million barrels of oil.

Partners in the development include operator Petro-Canada with 34.2 percent, Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada with 20.7 percent, Husky Oil Ltd with 15.8 percent, Norsk Hydro A/S with 15 percent, Murphy Oil Corp with 10.7 percent and Mosbacher Operating Co with 3.6 percent.
